<task>
Production incident with evidence released in 3 stages over time.
Read-only files are under /task/fixtures. Stage 1 is available now:
  stage-1/UPDATE.md (4 lines)
  stage-1/config/payments-api.yaml (14 lines)
  stage-1/deploy/deploys.log (7 lines)
  stage-1/deploy/release-notes-5.36.1-f33d.md (23 lines)
  stage-1/logs/ingress-a.log (433 lines)
  stage-1/logs/payments-api.log (862 lines)
  stage-1/ops/oncall-notes.md (6 lines)

Staged evidence:
- Reply {"action": "advance"} to release the next stage when you are ready. Its files appear
  under /task/fixtures/stage-N/ and an update message is added to your working context.
  Released files never change and stay readable for the rest of the task.
- A final answer is accepted only after all 3 stages are released.

Rules of evidence:
- Build release notes describe defaults shipped in a build; they override repository config files.
- Records marked APPLIED in change logs are authoritative and supersede release-note defaults,
  config files and earlier notes. If two authoritative records conflict, the later wins.
- PROPOSED records were not applied. On-call notes are informal and may be out of date.
- Earlier hypotheses may be superseded by later evidence; diagnose the incident as it stands at
  the end of the final stage.

Answer fields (all required):
- root_cause: start with exactly one cause code, then a colon and a one-sentence explanation.
- required_value: the exact current effective value of the setting at the centre of the root
  cause at the end of the final stage.
- remedy: start with exactly one remedy code, then a colon and a concrete action.
- evidence_refs: list of "path:line" or "path:start-end" references (paths relative to
  /task/fixtures, 1-based, ranges of at most 20 lines) supporting (1) the current symptom,
  (2) the record that sets the current effective value, and (3) the record of the change that
  originally introduced the problem.

Cause codes:
  DB_POOL_EXHAUSTED: database connection pool too small for load
  TLS_CERT_EXPIRED: an expired TLS certificate is being served or presented
  CLIENT_TIMEOUT_TOO_LOW: a client timeout is lower than the upstream's normal latency
  FEATURE_FLAG_REGRESSION: a feature flag rollout enabled faulty code
  DISK_FULL: a volume ran out of space
  DNS_RESOLUTION_FAILURE: service discovery / DNS records are wrong or failing
  MEMORY_LIMIT_OOM: processes are killed for exceeding memory limits
  UPSTREAM_RATE_LIMITED: an upstream is rejecting calls due to rate limits
Remedy codes:
  RAISE_DB_POOL_LIMIT: raise the connection pool limit to cover demand
  ROTATE_CERTIFICATE: deploy a valid, unexpired certificate
  RAISE_CLIENT_TIMEOUT: raise the client timeout above upstream latency
  DISABLE_FEATURE_FLAG: turn the faulty feature flag off
  EXPAND_VOLUME: free or expand the full volume
  FIX_DNS_RECORD: correct the DNS / discovery record
  RAISE_MEMORY_LIMIT: raise the memory limit or fix the leak
  REQUEST_RATE_LIMIT_INCREASE: reduce call rate or obtain a higher quota
</task>

The other deploys (shipping-api, billing-svc, orders-api, inventory-svc, quotes-api) look unrelated.\n- deploy/release-notes-5.36.1-f33d.md (overrides the repo config):\n  - line 13: default clients.risk-score.timeout_ms lowered 2500 -> 800 (\"fail fast\").\n  - line 16: default db.pool.max_size lowered 60 -> 14 \"to fit the shared-db connection quota\".\n  - line 9: ff-legacy-export removed (was 0%).\n  - Everything else is benign.\n- ops/oncall-notes.md (informal, may be stale):\n  - line 5: at 08:33, 5xx since 5.36.1-f33d with many risk-score timeouts.\n  - line 6: at 08:43, suspects the risk-score timeout change.\n- logs/payments-api.log background WARN noise:\n  - gc pauses 135-256ms\n  - \"dns cache refresh retry succeeded\" (line 7)\n  - TLS cert for payments-api.internal \"expires in 27 days\" (line 8)\n  - disk /var/data at 67% (line 25)\n\nError grep (ERROR lines or 5xx-looking lines):\n- logs/payments-api.log has only one error type: \"ERROR payments-api [payments-api-\u003cpod>] upstream call risk-score timed out after Nms (attempt...)\".\n  - first seen at line 179 (41 occurrences, pod d*)\n  - line 191 (29 occurrences, pod e*)\n  - line 222 (25 occurrences, pod a*)\n- No DB pool or acquire errors were found.\n- logs/ingress-a.log returned no matches with that filter. Its 5xx format probably differs; it has not been inspected yet.\n- Notes were saved to /task/workspace/notes.txt.\n\nHypotheses:\n- Leading: CLIENT_TIMEOUT_TOO_LOW. The risk-score timeout is 800ms per release notes line 13, and risk-score timeout errors are confirmed from line 179 onward.\n  - Still need the actual \"timed out after Nms\" value and the normal risk-score latency, to confirm latency is above 800ms.\n- DB_POOL_EXHAUSTED: unlikely so far, since there are no pool errors in stage 1. Recheck in later stages.\n- Ruled out: TLS (27 days left), DISK (67%), DNS (retry succeeded).\n\nNext steps:\n1. View payments-api.log around lines 175-200 to get the exact timeout ms and any latency values.\n2. Look at ingress-a.log for 5xx lines and their line numbers.\n3. Advance to stage 2, then stage 3. Look for APPLIED or PROPOSED records changing timeout_ms or pool max_size; the later APPLIED record wins, and PROPOSED records are ignored. The cause may shift in later stages.\n4. Final evidence_refs should include:\n   - a symptom log range, e.g. stage-1/logs/payments-api.log:179-198, or a later-stage log\n   - the record setting the current effective value\n   - the originating change, stage-1/deploy/release-notes-5.36.1-f33d.md:13 (or :16 if the cause turns out to be DB)"}
